profiles.name: soft (FROZEN, trial 28): catch-up on the crypto rules only (cap 3x) + cushion
profiles.plain: Each week starts at the normal stake. When the week is losing, only the five bitcoin / ether rules raise their stake (up to 3 times) to climb back; as soon as the week is winning, every rule bets small (a quarter of the normal stake, growing back as the week's gain grows) so the gain is not given back. The base stake is cut to 0.58 of the reference's so that the worst week stays the same.
profiles.frozen_rule: Code: /home/user/gold-orb/lab/r2/tracks/stake/stake.py, FROZEN['soft'] = {wk_cap 3, famcap (us100 1, gold 1, crypto 3), prot_k 4, prot_min 0.25}, base_scale 0.58. Clock: FP server time (New York + 7 h); week = Monday..Sunday; a result is booked at the trade's exit time. State w at a trade's entry = sum of (stake x R) of the trades closed STRICTLY before that entry inside the current server week, in units of the base stake. Stake multiplier m: if w < 0: crypto trades m = 1 + min(2, -w); us100 and gold trades m = 1. If w = 0: m = 1. If w > 0: m = min(1, max(0.25, w / 4)). Base stake = 0.58 x the reference's (0.58 % of the account if the reference is 1 %), so a trade risks between 0.145 % and 1.74 %. Entries, stops and exits of the ten rules untouched. Selected by the Addendum E rule among the configurations keeping >= 2/3 of the reference's total (gross, common period); 0.58 = smallest of the four scales (0.659 gross, 0.580 net).

profiles.name: cushion only (NOT FROZEN, information: trial 33): never more than the normal stake
profiles.plain: No catch-up at all. The only change: once the week is winning, every rule bets small (a quarter of the normal stake, back to normal once the week is 4 stakes ahead). It is not one of the two profiles the selection rule froze; it is listed because it is the cheapest step of the frontier and the only one that keeps the reference's worst week on a 1,000 EUR account.

design.frontier:
All figures computed by my script /home/user/gold-orb/lab/r2/tracks/stake/run.py (table in /home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/r2/stake/summary.json, key frontier_winning_weeks_vs_profit_kept_after_scaling), in sample, common period 2018-02..2021-12. "Worst week x" = worst week at an unchanged base stake as a multiple of the reference's; "profit kept" = total after the base stake is scaled down so the worst week equals the reference's; drawdown after scaling is below the reference's for every line (0.65-0.92x).

Trial | winning weeks without costs / with costs | worst week x | profit kept without / with costs | winning weeks with NO edge (zero-edge control)
01 reference | 61.2 % / 58.3 % | 1.00 | 100 % / 100 % | 49.9 %
16 cushion k2 | 65.5 / 64.1 | 0.94 | 99 / 93 | 54.7
33 cushion k4 (stake never above base) | 71.4 / 67.0 | 0.94 | 92 / 88 | 60.6
35 crypto catch-up 2x + cushion | 77.7 / 74.3 | 1.27 (1.42 net) | 82 / 73 | not run
28 SOFT crypto catch-up 3x + cushion | 79.6 / 75.2 | 1.52 (1.72 net) | 77 / 73 | 67.5
38 crypto 3x + us100 2x + cushion | 81.1 / 76.7 | 1.81 | 66 / 67 | 68.8
29 crypto and us100 3x + cushion | 82.5 / 77.7 | 2.13 | 58 / 60 | 70.0
36 STRONG crypto 5x, us100 3x + cushion | 84.0 / 79.1 | 2.55 | 56 / 59 | 72.4
37 crypto and us100 5x + cushion | 84.0 / 80.1 | 3.05 | 48 / 52 | not run
27 all rules 5x + cushion | 83.5 / 79.1 | 3.70 | 45 / 46 | not run

Reading: the first +9 to +10 points of winning weeks cost 8-12 % of the profit and no extra worst week (cushion alone). The next +8 points cost another ~15 % of the profit and a worst week 1.5-1.7x larger at an unchanged stake (or a base stake cut to 0.58). The last +4 points cost another ~15-20 % of the profit and a worst week 2.55x larger (base stake cut to 0.39). Beyond 5x nothing more is gained (84.0 %). With no edge at all the same ladder reads 49.9 % -> 60.6 % -> 67.5 % -> 72.4 %: the gain in winning weeks is almost entirely manufactured by the stake rule, and is paid by red weeks 1.5x, 2.1x and 2.6x larger than green ones.

Per week size at the frozen stakes, with costs: reference green +9.57 % / red -4.20 %; soft +5.25 % / -4.75 %; strong +4.12 % / -4.87 %.

Winning DAYS by stake rules alone: ceiling 57.3 % without costs / 55.2 % with (trial 32: stake 5x as soon as the day is red, stop for the day at the first gain), which fails the drawdown condition (1.03x) and keeps 46 % / 40 % of the profit, average green day +5.83 R against red -4.77 R. Best eligible: 56.2 % / 54.2 % (trial 04, day catch-up 5x), profit kept 59 % / 50 %. Reference 50.9 % / 49.6 %. The frozen profiles reach 52.7 % / 50.6 % (soft) and 53.3 % / 52.0 % (strong). Stake rules do not produce green days: +1 to +6 points at most.
dead_ends: Stake rules for green DAYS (trials 02-05, 31, 32): day catch-up 2x / 3x / 5x gives 53.7 / 55.7 / 56.2 % of days without costs (52.1 / 53.6 / 54.2 % with), winning weeks unchanged (59.7-62.1 %), profit kept after scaling 88 / 86 / 59 % (85 / 75 / 50 % with costs). Adding it on top of the week rule changes nothing (82.0 % of weeks with or without it, 53.8 % vs 53.4 % of days).

Daily profit lock (trials 05, 32): +0.5 R lock with day catch-up 3x: 56.1 % of days gross, fails the drawdown condition with costs (1.14x). Lock at the first gain with 5x step: 57.3 % of days, weeks fall to 57.3 %, months to 70.8 %, drawdown 1.03x: not eligible.

Weekly profit lock (trials 07, 15): stop for the week at +3 R alone: 63.6 % of weeks gross (60.2 % net) for 19-21 % of the profit, not eligible gross (drawdown 1.00x after scaling up). Lock at +2 R added to catch-up 3x: 78.0 % vs 77.7 % gross, profit kept 50 % vs 60 %.

Weekly loss stop (trials 13, 14): catch-up 3x with no new trade after -8 R or -12 R: worst week cut to 1.3-1.65x so the base stake is scaled up, and the drawdown then exceeds the reference's with costs (1.36x and 1.24x): not eligible in the net view; winning weeks 69.9 % and 75.2 % gross.

Smaller stake after a green week (trials 21, 25): half stake after a green week alone: 60.7 % of weeks (reference 61.2 %), drawdown 1.13x after scaling: not eligible. Added to catch-up + cushion it lowers winning weeks from 80.1 % to 76.7 %.
Catch-up on every rule except crypto (trial 22): 68.9 % of weeks gross / 63.6 % net for a worst week 1.9x; limit on the total of boosted open trades (trial 24): 69.9 % / 66.5 %. Both dominated.

Step formula (trials 08, 09: full multiplier as soon as the week is red) is no better than the linear one: 76.2 % vs 77.7 % at 3x for a larger worst week (2.84x vs 2.59x). Slower catch-up (trial 10, one extra stake per 3 R lost): 74.8 %.
Cushion variants (trials 19, 26, 39): floor at 0.1 instead of 0.25: no change (80.6 vs 80.1 %); slope 6 instead of 4: same weeks, less profit; floor at 0.5: 78.6 % gross but 71.4 % net vs 75.2 %.

Crypto correlation measured: daily results correlate 0.62 (F1 btc / F1 eth), 0.41 (brk72 btc / eth), 0.34 (the two us100 rules), 0.016 on average for the other pairs; the five crypto rules carry 64 % of the weekly variance. In sample the catch-up on crypto only looks efficient (74.8 % of weeks, 87 % of the profit kept); with no edge it is NOT: 58.5 % of weeks for a median worst week of -51.8 R, against 58.4 % for -40.5 R when the catch-up is on us100 and gold only. Linking the crypto trades in the draw makes worst weeks about 1.3x larger for every variant.

A dedicated small-account mechanism was not found: on 1,000 EUR the minimum lots already turn each profile into 'small trades when green, larger ones when red', and that degraded form is what is reported. Raising the base stake to let more trades through raises the worst week in proportion (soft at 1.16 %: 44 % of signals, worst week -22 %; at 1.74 %: 58 %, -33 %).
design.honest_summary:
Two profiles are frozen by the Addendum E rule, in sample only; nothing was run on 2022-2025 and the lead's validation look is still to do. All figures are computed by /home/user/gold-orb/lab/r2/tracks/stake/run.py; 39 of the 40 allowed configurations are logged in /home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/r2/stake/trials.jsonl, the seven of the first scout first (my engine reproduces Addendum E's 49.6 / 58.3 / 85.4 % exactly).

- **Winning weeks:** with costs, 58.3 % becomes 75.2 % (soft) or 79.1 % (strong); without costs, 61.2 % becomes 79.6 % or 84.0 %. The longest run of red weeks falls from 7 to 2.
- **Winning days:** stake rules do not deliver them. The profiles sit at 50.6-52.0 % with costs (reference 49.6 %), and the best any stake rule reached is 54-57 %.
- **The price in sample:** the base stake is cut to 0.58 (soft) or 0.39 (strong) of the reference's to keep the same worst week, and 73-77 % or 56-59 % of the profit remains. The average green week shrinks from +9.6 % to +5.3 % or +4.1 %, while the average red week stays near -4.8 %.
- **The gain is not edge:** on the same trades with no edge, the rules still show 67.5 % and 72.4 % winning weeks against 49.9 %. They rearrange results into many small green weeks and fewer, larger red ones (2.1x and 2.6x the green ones when there is no edge).
- **Ruin risk:** at the frozen stakes the zero-edge chance of losing half the account in 4 years is 50 % and 46 %, against 61 % for the reference at 1 %. It is 70 % and 77 % if the base stake is left at 1 %.
- **1,000 EUR:** neither profile can be executed as designed. At today's prices the minimum lots let through about 25 % of the signals (42 % for the reference itself). The degraded form still showed 77 % winning weeks in sample against 61 %, with the soft profile's worst week 1.5x the reference's on that account. As designed: about 20,000 EUR (soft), 20,000-50,000 EUR (strong), about 5,000 EUR for the reference.

Weak points the lead should know:
- The winner changes with the view: with costs the rule picks trials 37 and 38, on 2013-2021 trials 27 and 28 / 35. All are neighbours (cushion plus catch-up on crypto and us100); the frozen ones follow the view I declared before running anything (without costs, 2018-2021).
- The "soft" definition (keep at least 2/3 of the profit) is mine, written before the search; Addendum E's rule alone yields only the strong one.
- Putting the catch-up on crypto looks efficient only because crypto carries the largest in-sample edge; with no edge it is not more efficient than the other families.
- The literal zero-edge draw (random sign) turns large winners into large losers, so its worst weeks (-26 % median for the reference) are about twice the real one (-12.5 %). I added a shape-keeping draw; both are in the summary.
- The yearly percentages are in-sample results of rules chosen on that sample, an upper bound and not a forecast.
- While listing files I printed the head of /home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/r2/round3_summary.json, which contains the reference's aggregate 2022-2025 figures. No stake rule is involved and no choice used it.
- A few exploratory account runs at other base stakes are in scratch scripts only (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/vert/mise/acc1.py and acc3.py); no selection was made on them.

For the validation look: build the frame with `stake.build_frame({(name, sym): trades})`, then `account.account(S.FROZEN[p]['config'], 1000.0, base_pct=1.0 * S.FROZEN[p]['base_scale'], d=account.frame(d=frame))` against `account.account({}, 1000.0, 1.0, d=...)`. On 1,000 EUR both will be partial because of the minimum lots; a 20,000 EUR run gives the as-designed reading.

NOT REPRODUCED / WRONG IN THE PROPOSAL: "73 % (with costs) to 77 % (without) of the profit kept" for soft: at the frozen 0.58 base it is 68 % without costs (168 / 246); 77 % belongs to the per-view scale 0.659, not to the frozen base. findings.evidence: Weeks are counted on closed trades only (result booked at exit). 144 gold trades (21 % of the two gold breakout rules) are still open at the Friday close and their loss or gain is pushed to the next week. Marking open trades at the last in-sample price before the week end (a5.py, with costs): reference 59.2 %, soft 71.4 %, strong 75.7 %, cushion 66.0 %. 15 to 24 weeks change sign. The gain on what the user sees as equity on Friday night is +12, +16.5, +7 points. Second effect: the rule resets on Monday, so it makes Monday-to-Friday weeks green and nothing else. Same P&L read on 7-day windows ending Monday to Thursday (a2.py): soft 65.9-68.9 % against reference 60.7-64.9 % (+2 to +8 points); strong 66.3-70.9 %; cushion 60.5-65.9 %. Two-week blocks: 77.7 % soft against 67.0 %; four-week blocks 84.6 % against 78.8 %; months 83.3 % against 85.4 %.
findings.corrected_number: Equity-based winning weeks, with costs: reference 59.2 %, soft 71.4 %, strong 75.7 %, cushion 66.0 %.

findings.claim: "The base stake is cut so that the worst week stays the same" (-12.5 % for all).
findings.evidence: True for one week out of 206, which is the week the scale was fitted on. The rest of the bad tail is fatter (a4.py, with costs, frozen bases): weeks worse than -8 %: reference 9, soft 11, strong 12; worse than -10 %: 5, 7, 6; 5th-percentile week -7.6 % (reference), -8.8 % (soft), -8.3 % (strong). The fair yardstick is the reference at the flat stake that earns the same in-sample profit: 0.73 % for soft gives worst week -9.1 %, 2 weeks below -8 %, average red week -3.05 % (soft -4.75 %); 0.59 % for strong gives worst week -7.4 %, 0 weeks below -8 %. So for the same money soft's worst week is 1.38x larger and strong's 1.71x. In 103 of 206 weeks soft reaches the 3x cap on crypto; 45 of its 51 red weeks are such weeks; the rule turned 37 red weeks green and made 33 red weeks worse by 3.0 % on average.
findings.corrected_number: Weeks worse than -8 %: 11 (soft), 12 (strong), 9 (reference at 1 %), 2 (reference at the flat 0.73 % stake that earns as much as soft).

findings.claim: Zero-edge chance of losing half the account: 50 % (soft) and 46 % (strong) "against 61 % for the reference at 1 %".
findings.evidence: The comparison only reflects the smaller base stake. Same draws (a3.py, random sign, 1,000 draws): reference at flat 0.58 % loses half in 37.7 % of draws, at 0.39 % in 21.5 %, at 0.73 % (same in-sample profit as soft) in 46.7 %; soft at 0.58 % in 52.6 %, strong at 0.39 % in 47.0 %. Shape-keeping resampling: soft 54.3 %, strong 51.3 %, reference at 0.73 % 48.6 %, at 0.59 % 38.9 %. The stake rule does not lower the risk of ruin; at an equal stake or an equal profit it raises it.

findings.evidence: Real order of the trades, each result reduced by half its rule's mean (a4.py), with costs / without costs. Reference: 50.0 / 49.5 % weeks, +101 / +123 %/yr, worst week -14.2 %, drawdown 42.1 %, months 58.3 %. Strong @0.39: 70.9 / 73.8 %, +55 / +76 %/yr, worst week -15.1 %, drawdown 36.6 % (1.59x the flat-stake reference of equal profit), green +3.88, red -5.84. Cushion: 58.3 / 58.7 %, +71 / +94 %/yr, worst week -14.0 %, drawdown 34.8 %. With independent resampling at half edge the levels are higher for everything (reference 56.9 %, soft 72.5 %, strong 76.4 %, cushion 66.0 %) but the gain is the same: +15 to +16 (soft), +19 to +21 (strong), +8 to +9 (cushion). findings.claim: Zero-edge control: "67.5 %, 72.4 %, 60.6 % winning weeks with no edge against 49.9 %".
findings.evidence: The control is done and reproduces, but the level is flattered by the draw: a random sign turns the rules' long winners into long losers and independent draws erase the link between the crypto rules. Check: the same independent draws at the FULL in-sample edge give the reference 74.2 % (sign) or 68.6 % (resampling) winning weeks, while the real sequence shows 58.3 %. On the real order of the trades with each rule's mean removed (one path, a4.py, with costs): reference 44.7 %, soft 53.9 %, strong 61.2 %, cushion 48.5 %; average red week -6.4 % against green +5.1 % for soft; total -12 %/yr (soft), -18 %/yr (strong) on that path. What is stable across the three readings is the gain manufactured by the rule: +9 to +17 points (soft), +16 to +22 (strong), +4 to +11 (cushion).

findings.claim: On 1,000 EUR the "degraded form still showed 77 % winning weeks against 61 %".
findings.evidence: The degraded form is another robot (a6.py, today's prices, with costs). Soft takes 1,345 trades of 5,207: 1,018 are the two ether rules (506 of 511 and 512 of 516), 314 are bitcoin trades that pass only when tripled, 12 are Nasdaq, 1 is gold, the Friday-gold and Donchian-gold rules never trade. Risk of one minimum lot: ether 0.5-0.8 EUR, bitcoin 9-18 EUR, Nasdaq 12-14 EUR, gold 18-29 EUR, against a budget of 5.8 EUR (1.45 EUR when the week is green, 17.4 EUR at 3x). Not shown by the designer: winning months 74.5 % (soft) and 78.7 % (strong) against 85.1 % for the reference on the same account; soft's worst week is -10.5 % against -6.8 %, 1.54x, above the 1.25x limit Addendum E sets for an offer; at 2018-2021 prices it is strong that breaks it (-12.8 % against -9.5 %, 1.35x). Strong gives the same 77.1 % of weeks as soft for +59 %/yr instead of +79 %/yr. The reference at a flat 0.58 % on that account: 53.2 % weeks, +39 %/yr, worst week -3.3 %. findings.claim: Catch-up placed on crypto; correlated positions.
findings.evidence: a7.py and a2.py: crypto carries 75 % of the in-sample profit (594 of 787 R; mean 0.194 R per trade against 0.108 Nasdaq and 0.064 gold). Trades staked at 2x or more are 17.6 % of soft's trades and bring 52 % of its profit (24.3 % and 66 % for strong): the profit kept depends on the crypto edge holding exactly when the stake is raised. Crypto trades entered in a green week, where the cushion cuts the stake to a quarter, had the highest mean in sample (0.302 R against 0.181 R in a red week). Risk open at once at the frozen bases: up to 8.7 % of the account in five crypto positions for soft, 9.75 % for strong, against 5 % for the reference at 1 %; all markets 10.4 %, 12.5 %, 9.0 %. No crypto trade is held over a weekend.

Followed in substance: 39 of 40 configurations logged, selection reproduces from the log, both zero-edge controls present. Reservations: (1) the selection view (without costs, 2018-2021) and the "soft" definition (keep >= 2/3) are the designer's own; the files are untracked in git so "written before any run" cannot be checked; with costs the same rule picks trials 37 and 38, on 2013-2021 with costs 27 and 35, and soft at the frozen 0.58 keeps only 64.6 % of the profit there. (2) The 39 trials were run in six batches, each informed by the previous one; the top five differ by 0.5 to 2 points while the sampling error of a weekly share on 206 weeks is about +/-5 points (week bootstrap, a4.py: soft 70.4-80.1 %). (3) The without-cost re-run used frames cut at 2022-01-15, and the saved trades include exits up to 2022-01-03 of trades entered in December 2021 (one week labelled 2022). (4) The designer printed the head of round3_summary.json with aggregate 2022-2025 reference figures, disclosed. (5) The 1,000 EUR table uses his own variant of the account loop and a rescaling to today's prices, neither in Addendum E; at 2018-2021 prices the same account takes 60 % of soft's signals, not 25.8 %. (6) The cushion profile is not frozen and Addendum E gives it no validation look.

per_profile_verdict.why: Every headline figure reproduces and no look-ahead was found. It does buy Monday-to-Friday green weeks, in sample and at half the edge. Three things in the proposal must be corrected before the user sees it: the gain is +12 points on equity, not +17; "same worst week" hides more bad weeks and a worst week 1.38x that of a flat stake earning the same; the ruin comparison is against a reference staked 1.7 times higher. On his 1,000 EUR it runs as an ether robot with a bitcoin catch-up, and its in-sample worst week there is 1.54x the reference's, above Addendum E's 1.25x offer limit.
